title.rendered: Let the Peace of Christ Rule, and Be Thankful: The Umpire of the Heart | The Thankful Heart, Day 6

excerpt.rendered: Colossians 3:15 tells us to let the peace of God rule in our hearts and to be thankful. Day 6 of The Thankful Heart lets peace be the umpire.

content.rendered:
Every heart has an inner referee. Fear wants the whistle. Worry wants the whistle. Paul says give it to the peace of Christ, and then he adds three small words that keep it there: and be thankful.

The Gospel For Today | Friday, November 20, 2026 | The Thankful Heart, Day 6

Today’s Scripture

“And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to which also you were called in one body; and be thankful.”
Colossians 3:15 (NKJV)

“And whatever you do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him.”
Colossians 3:17 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

The NKJV reads “the peace of God,” and many other translations read “the peace of Christ.” Both point to the same gift: the peace Jesus left with His disciples when He said His peace was His gift to them, not as the world gives (John 14:27). This peace is not a mood we work up. It is a Person who lives in us.

The word Paul uses for “rule” comes from the world of the games. It describes the umpire, the one who makes the call. When two voices compete inside you, one saying “panic” and the other saying “trust,” Paul says let the peace of Christ decide. Let it blow the whistle. Let it have the final word over the decision, the conversation, the news report, the late payment.

And notice how the verse ends: “and be thankful.” That is not a random add-on. Thanksgiving is what keeps peace on the referee’s stand. Worry looks at what might go wrong. Thanksgiving looks at what God has already done. It is very hard to stay anxious while you are counting His faithfulness out loud. Philippians 4:6-7 joins the same two things: prayer with thanksgiving, and then the peace of God guarding our hearts.

Paul also says we were “called in one body.” Peace and thankfulness are not only private. They shape how we treat each other. A thankful church in Lagos or a thankful family in London is a place where peace can rule, because people are too busy noticing the grace of God in one another to keep score. Then verse 17 widens it to everything: whatever you do, in word or deed, “giving thanks to God the Father through Him.”

So today, when the inner argument starts, try this. Stop and give thanks for one specific thing God has already done in that very area. Thank Him for His presence in it, His past faithfulness in it, His promise over it. Then let His peace make the call. You will find the whistle was always in His hand.

How the Thankful Heart Stays at Peace

It lets Christ’s peace make the call. Fear and worry do not get the final word.

It keeps peace in place with thanks. Gratitude for what God has done quiets anxiety about what might happen.

It spreads peace to others. We are called in one body, and thankful people make peaceful homes and churches.

Declaration

Lord Jesus, I thank You that You have given me Your peace, not as the world gives (John 14:27). I let Your peace rule in my heart and make the call over every decision, and I am thankful (Colossians 3:15). I thank You that Your peace, which surpasses all understanding, guards my heart and mind through Christ Jesus (Philippians 4:7). Whatever I do in word or deed, I do in Your name, giving thanks to the Father through You. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
